title: 中国现代化进程的多维评估：混合 PCA–Stacking 框架

sections.text:
Frontiers in Economics and Management Volume 1 Issue 1, 2020
ISSN: 2692-7608 DOI: 10.6938/FEM.202001_1(1).0001

 A Hybrid PCA-Stacking Framework for Multidimensional
 Assessment of Development Trajectories: Evidence from China's
 Modernization Process
 Hanrui Wang1, Yile Wang1,*
 1 School of Economics, Beijing Technology and Business University, Beijing 102488, China.

 * Corresponding Author

Abstract
China's multidimensional modernization since 2000 necessitates comprehensive
assessment frameworks. This study constructs a novel China Development Index (CDI)
through integrated analytical approaches. Principal Component Analysis first distilled
14 indicators across economic, social, and governance domains into two dominant
components explaining 94.39% cumulative variance: an innovation-education-
governance nexus (84.88% weight) and economic fundamentals (15.12% weight).
Using Nonlinear Autoregressive Neural Network (NAR) neural networks optimized via
Levenberg-Marquardt algorithms (12 hidden neurons, 2-step delays), secondary
indicators like service sector growth were forecasted with 0.026 MSE. Stacking fusion
modeling combining Linear Regression, k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Random Forest
base learners then projected primary indicators, achieving 93.02 Mean Squared Error
(MSE) – 7.2% lower than individual models.
The entropy weight-variation coefficient method synthesized these projections into the
CDI, revealing three historical phases: Founding (1949-1978), Reform (1978-2000), and
Modernization (2000-2022). Longitudinal analysis demonstrates accelerated
development post-2000, with projections to 2062 indicating transition toward
sustainable development characterized by environmental decoupling. A Stacking
classification model integrating LightGBM, XGBoost, and Support Vector Machine (SVM)
achieved 95.6% accuracy in phase identification.

Keywords
Principal Component Analysis, China Development Index, NAR Neural Network, Stacking
Ensemble Modeling, Sustainable Development Transition, Phase Identification Model,
Entropy Weight-Variation Coefficient.

1. Introduction
China's modernization trajectory since 2000 encompasses intricate advancements across
political institutions, economic systems, and social welfare frameworks. This multidimensional
evolution—characterized by technological innovation, environmental governance upgrades,
and global cooperation initiatives—demands systematic assessment methodologies capable of
quantifying developmental complexities. Traditional economic indicators such as GDP growth
fail to capture institutional progress or sustainability transitions, creating significant
measurement gaps in policy formulation processes.
To address this research void, we establish an integrated analytical framework combining
dimensionality reduction techniques and machine learning fusion. Principal Component
Analysis (PCA) serves as the foundational methodology for distilling 14 critical indicators into
core development dimensions, elucidating dominant factors driving modernization processes.
Subsequent forecasting phases employ Nonlinear Autoregressive Neural Network (NAR)

neural networks optimized via Levenberg-Marquardt algorithms for time-series prediction of
secondary indicators[1], while Stacking ensemble modeling integrates multiple regression
techniques to enhance primary indicator projection accuracy.
The synthesis of these projections culminates in the China Development Index (CDI)—a novel
metric weighted through entropy-variation coefficient integration—which quantifies
developmental progress across historical epochs. Crucially, our approach identifies three
distinct modernization phases through systematic trend analysis, with empirical evidence
indicating an emergent sustainability transition period.
Methodologically, this study advances development economics through four innovations: first,
PCA application verifies that merely two principal components explain 94.39% of systemic
variance, with economic fundamentals (15.12% weight) and innovation-governance-education
integration (84.88% weight) constituting the core modernization drivers;second, NAR neural
networks achieve 0.026 Mean Squared Error (MSE) in secondary indicator forecasting through
12-neuron/2-delay architectures; third, Stacking fusion reduces primary indicator prediction
error by 7.2% versus standalone models[2]; finally, the entropy-variation coefficient weighting
system dynamically adjusts indicator importance to mitigate outlier sensitivity.
The ensuing CDI framework consequently provides policymakers with three critical capacities:
longitudinal progress tracking since 1949, evidence-based phase identification (validated at
95.6% accuracy), and scientifically-grounded sustainability transition forecasting. This
research thereby bridges theoretical econometrics and practical governance through a
replicable development assessment paradigm.

2. Literature Review
2.1. Theoretical Evolution of Modernization Metrics
Early development assessments predominantly relied on economic indicators such as GDP
growth and industrialization rates. This unidimensional approach proved inadequate for
capturing institutional progress and social welfare dimensions. Subsequent studies introduced
composite indices—notably the Human Development Index (HDI) by UNDP (1990)—
incorporating education and life expectancy metrics. However, these frameworks remained
limited in quantifying governance efficacy or environmental sustainability. The emergence of
multidimensional index systems (e.g., OECD’s Better Life Index) marked a paradigm shift,
emphasizing interactive effects between economic, social, and institutional variables. In China’s
context, Liu & Wang identified four modernization pillars through factor analysis: political
institution building[3], market liberalization, cultural capital accumulation, and educational
advancement. Their PCA application revealed that 78% of variance in provincial development
data stemmed from these interconnected dimensions. As Fig. 1 illustrates through its distinct
inflection point, PCA-based dimensionality reduction became pivotal for identifying dominant
factors—Liu & Wang demonstrated that 78% variance in provincial development data could
be explained by just two principal components:

2.2. Methodological Advancements in Development Forecasting
Predictive modeling for socioeconomic trajectories has evolved through three generations:
1. Econometric Foundations: Vector Autoregression (VAR) models dominated early
 development forecasting, yet struggled with nonlinear trend capture. Zhang’s NAR neural
 network application in manufacturing growth prediction demonstrated 32% higher
 accuracy than VAR alternatives, establishing neural networks’ superiority in complex
 system modeling[4].
2. Hybrid Approaches: Integration of dimensionality reduction and machine learning
 emerged as a critical innovation. Yang et al. combined PCA with Random Forests to forecast
 sustainability transitions, reducing prediction error by 19% through eliminating
 multicollinearity effects. This methodology directly informed our PCA-Stacking fusion
 framework.
3. Ensemble Learning Breakthroughs: Stacking algorithms gained prominence by integrating
 heterogeneous base learners. Chen’s research on East Asian development trajectories
 demonstrated that Stacking regression achieved 89.7% forecast accuracy by leveraging
 complementary strengths of tree-based models and kernel methods.
2.3. Critical Research Gaps
Three limitations persist in contemporary literature:
⚫ Temporal-Spatial Decoupling: Most indices (e.g., HDI) fail to dynamically weight indicators
 across development phases. The static structure of existing metrics cannot reflect China’s
 transition from investment-driven growth to innovation-centric development (post-2000).
⚫ Methodological Fragmentation: While PCA effectively reduces dimensionality, and neural
 networks excel at time-series forecasting, no study has integrated these into a unified
 prediction-classification framework[5].
⚫ Validation Deficits: Phase identification models lack rigorous accuracy testing. Traditional
 periodization relies on historiographical analysis rather than empirical thresholds.

3. Core Modernization Factor Extraction
The identification of pivotal modernization drivers begins with establishing a comprehensive
indicator system spanning economic, institutional, social, and environmental dimensions.
Fourteen core metrics—including GDP growth rate (calculated as percentage change between
consecutive periods), technological innovation index (weighted sum of R&D expenditure and
patent output)[6], and environmental quality index (derived from multi-pollutant AQI
computations)—undergo min-max normalization to ensure dimensional homogeneity. This
systematic approach captures modernization's inherent complexity while providing
standardized inputs for subsequent analysis.
Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is then rigorously executed through a sequential analytical
protocol. The computational workflow initiates with constructing a correlation matrix
quantifying inter-indicator relationships, followed by eigenvalue decomposition to extract
latent dimensions. Component retention adheres to the empirical criterion of cumulative
explained variance exceeding 90%, with the resultant principal components calculated as
linear combinations of original variables. This dimensionality reduction methodology
effectively distills multifaceted modernization dynamics into interpretable orthogonal factors.
The PCA output reveals two dominant components collectively explaining 94.39% of systemic
variance. The primary component (PC1), capturing 84.88% variance, exhibits strong loadings
on education level (0.089), technological innovation (0.088), and institutional quality (0.088),
signifying a cohesive innovation-governance nexus. This pattern is visually confirmed through
the factor loading heatmap, as the fig.2 shows, where deep red clusters demonstrate significant
institutional-educational synergy:

 Figure 2: Cross-cultural governance factors exhibit distinct clustering patterns
The secondary component (PC2), accounting for 15.12% variance, is predominantly driven by
economic fundamentals—GDP growth (0.478) and per capita income (0.478)—indicating that
traditional economic metrics remain vital yet comparatively less influential than institutional
factors in modernization progression. Statistical analysis further demonstrates these
components' operational independence, evidenced by their near-zero correlation coefficient (r
= -0.12), suggesting economic advancement and institutional innovation may progress along
distinct developmental trajectories.

Three paradigm-shifting insights emerge from this structural decomposition: First, the 5.6-fold
greater explanatory power of institutional factors (PC1) versus economic metrics (PC2)
establishes governance quality as modernization's primary catalyst. Second, environmental
sustainability indicators display weak cross-loadings (PC1: 0.081, PC2: -0.114), highlighting the
persistent challenge of ecological integration within core development frameworks[7]. Third,
the orthogonal relationship between development dimensions enables targeted policy
interventions, allowing strategic prioritization of institutional innovation without
compromising economic advancement.
This factor extraction framework fundamentally reorients modernization theory by
quantifying the relative contributions of distinct development vectors, establishing empirical
foundations for balanced, multi-dimensional progress assessment. The methodology's
robustness is further evidenced by its capacity to reduce complex multivariate interactions into
interpretable, policy-actionable dimensions while maintaining comprehensive system
representation

4. China Development Index Construction
4.1. Hierarchical Forecasting Architecture
The CDI construction initiates with a two-tiered predictive system integrating temporal pattern
recognition and ensemble learning. Secondary indicators (e.g., service sector growth) are
forecasted using Nonlinear Autoregressive (NAR) neural networks optimized via Levenberg-
Marquardt algorithms. For service sector value-added growth, a 12-neuron architecture with
2-step delays achieves 0.026 mean squared error, as the fig.3 shows, validated through rigorous
error diagnostics:

 Figure 3: Optimal NAR Neural Network Structure
Primary indicators (GDP growth, innovation index, etc.) are projected through Stacking fusion
modeling, combining Linear Regression, k-Nearest Neighbors (k=5), and Random Forest (150
estimators) base learners with a Linear Regression meta-learner. The multi-stage validation
confirms Stacking's superiority with 93.02 MSE[8], demonstrating 7.2% error reduction
compared to standalone models. As illustrated in Fig. 4, the optimized 12-neuron architecture
with 2-step delays demonstrates efficient learning dynamics:

4.2. Adaptive Weighting Mechanism
Indicator importance is dynamically calibrated through dual complementary methodologies:
entropy weighting quantifies informational significance based on dispersion patterns, while
variation coefficient analysis measures temporal stability across developmental phases. The
synthesized weighting system (λ=0.5) reveals modernization's multidimensional essence—
economic indicators collectively command 27% influence while institutional and social
dimensions dominate at 58% aggregate weighting. This sophisticated balancing ensures the
CDI accurately reflects evolving priorities without overemphasizing transient economic
fluctuations[9].

Historical analysis of the CDI trajectory (1949-2022) identifies three distinct developmental
epochs: The Founding Era (1949-1978) exhibits CDI stagnation between 0.28–0.35, reflecting
institutional establishment challenges; the Reform Acceleration period (1978-2000)
demonstrates steady ascent from 0.42 to 0.68, signaling market liberalization benefits; and the
Modernization Surge (2000-2022) reveals exponential growth to 0.92, confirming innovation-
driven transformation. Crucially, the post-2000 period shows 214% CDI expansion versus 52%
GDP growth, as the fig.5 shows, evidencing multidimensional progress beyond economic

4.4. Sustainability Transition Thresholding
Projections to 2062 indicate an imminent Green Sustainable Development Era characterized by
environmental decoupling, innovation-driven growth, and regional convergence. Empirical
simulations identify CDI≥0.95 for three consecutive years as the sustainability transition
threshold—projected for attainment by 2043±2 years based on Monte Carlo modeling.
Validation against alternative indices demonstrates CDI's superior stability during global
crises[10], maintaining <5% deviation versus 15-22% volatility in conventional economic
metrics, establishing its robustness as a next-generation development assessment framework.
4.5. Theoretical Advancements
This research pioneers four paradigm-shifting contributions: First, it establishes the first
unified analytical framework integrating PCA dimensionality reduction, neural network
forecasting, and Stacking fusion; second[11], the adaptive weighting mechanism dynamically
recalibrates indicator importance according to developmental phase transitions; third,
quantifiable sustainability thresholds provide actionable policy targets; finally, the transferable
methodology offers global applicability for multidimensional progress assessment beyond the
Chinese context.
The CDI construction fundamentally reorients development economics by transcending
economic reductionism—instead embedding institutional quality, innovation capacity, and
environmental stewardship into a dynamically balanced assessment system. Its hierarchical
architecture and predictive robustness provide policymakers with unprecedented capabilities
for strategic planning, while its longitudinal validation confirms capacity to navigate complex
developmental transitions from industrialization through digital transformation toward
sustainable modernization.

5. Development Phase Identification
5.1. Historical Context and Analytical Imperative
China's developmental journey manifests distinct evolutionary phases characterized by shifting
policy priorities and socioeconomic transformations. Three empirically defined epochs emerge
from longitudinal analysis: The Founding Era (1949-1978) established institutional

foundations amid industrialization drives; the Reform Acceleration Period (1978-2000)
catalyzed market liberalization and global integration; while the Modernization Surge (2000-
2022) propelled technological innovation and social welfare enhancement. These phases
exhibit unique developmental signatures across economic structure, institutional quality, and
environmental engagement metrics, providing the categorical foundation for algorithmic
recognition[12].
5.2. Stacking Classification Framework Architecture
The phase identification system employs a sophisticated multi-layered fusion model
integrating heterogeneous classifiers. The base layer incorporates five complementary
algorithms: LightGBM implements Leaf-Wise growth optimization for efficient tree splitting:
XGBoost provides parallel tree construction capabilities, while Random Forest introduces
diversity through feature bagging. SVM delivers high-dimensional separation, with Logistic
Regression ensuring probabilistic calibration. These base predictions are synthesized through
a Gradient Boosting meta-classifier, creating a hierarchical decision architecture that leverages
each algorithm's comparative advantages.
5.3. Model Optimization and Validation
Hyperparameter refinement utilizes comprehensive grid search with 5-fold cross-validation,
identifying optimal configurations that balance complexity and generalization. The LightGBM
component achieves peak performance with 31 leaves and 0.05 learning rate, while XGBoost
operates optimally at depth-3 trees. The integrated system demonstrates exceptional
discriminative capability, as evidenced by progressive accuracy enhancement during training.
The integration of machine learning fusion with developmental theory establishes new
standards for evidence-based historical analysis, creating unprecedented capabilities for
predictive governance and strategic planning in complex socioeconomic transitions.

6. Conclusion
This study establishes the China Development Index (CDI) through an integrated PCA-Stacking-
NAR framework, capturing modernization's multidimensional essence. Principal Component
Analysis revealed two dominant drivers: an innovation-governance-education nexus (84.88%
weight) and economic fundamentals (15.12% weight), jointly explaining 94.39% systemic
variance. The hierarchical forecasting architecture demonstrated exceptional precision, with
NAR networks achieving 0.026 MSE for secondary indicators and Stacking fusion reducing
primary indicator error by 7.2%.
Longitudinal CDI trajectory analysis empirically validated three developmental phases: the
institution-building Founding Era (1949-1978), market-liberalizing Reform Acceleration
(1978-2000), and innovation-driven Modernization Surge (2000-2022). The post-2000 period
shows CDI growth (214%) significantly outpacing GDP expansion (52%), confirming
multidimensional progress beyond economic metrics:
The Stacking classification model achieved 95.6% phase recognition accuracy through
LightGBM/XGBoost/SVM fusion, precisely delineating historical transitions while projecting an
imminent Green Sustainable Development Era characterized by environmental decoupling and
regional convergence. This transition is quantified at CDI≥0.95 threshold attainment by 2043±2
years:
Theoretically, this research pioneers four advances: a unified analytical framework integrating
dimensionality reduction and ensemble learning; dynamic weighting balancing economic
(27%), institutional (58%), and environmental (15%) priorities; algorithmic periodization
replacing subjective historiography; and quantifiable sustainability thresholds. Practically, CDI

title: 基于双重机器学习的投资者情绪对 IPO 定价效率影响研究

Research on the Impact of Investor Sentiment on IPO Pricing Efficiency Based on Double Machine Learning

Jintai Ye
Jinan University-University of Birmingham Joint Institute

Guangzhou, China

School of Finance and Trade

Abstract—Against the backdrop of deepening registration-based reform and increasing volatility in capital market sentiment, research on the mechanisms affecting IPO pricing efficiency holds both significant theoretical value and practical relevance. Drawing on behavioral finance and information economics, this paper employs the Double Machine Learning (DML) framework and Generalized Random Forests (GRF) to conduct a systematic empirical analysis of A-share IPOs from 2019 to 2023. The findings indicate that investor sentiment exerts a significant positive effect on IPO underpricing, and this conclusion remains robust across a series of sensitivity tests. Further moderation analysis reveals that issuance size negatively moderates the sentiment–underpricing relationship through liquidity dilution and investor structure optimization, while daily price fluctuation limits amplify the effect of sentiment due to delayed price discovery. The heterogeneity analysis further demonstrates that issuance size plays a dominant moderating role: smaller offerings are more susceptible to sentiment-driven mispricing, whereas larger issues exhibit greater pricing stability. Issuance P/E ratio presents an inverted-U effect, with sentiment impact peaking at moderate valuation levels. Earnings per share displays a nonlinear pattern, where low-profit or loss-making firms are more sentiment-sensitive, while stronger profitability weakens the marginal influence of sentiment. Overall, this study uncovers the complexity and nonlinearity of sentiment effects on IPO pricing efficiency and provides solid theoretical and empirical evidence for enhancing pricing mechanisms under the registration-based system.
Keywords—Double Machine Learning, Generalized Random Forests, IPO underpricing,sensitivity tests 
Introduction 
The IPO premium phenomenon has long been prevalent in global stock markets, particularly in China's A-share market, where it has

been especially pronounced, making it a focal point of academic research. Scholars have explored IPO premiums from various angles, considering rational factors such as market segmentation theory, exchange rates and systemic risk, as well as irrational factors such as investor sentiment. According to the behavioural finance school of thought, investor sentiment is a key participant in market transactions and is closely linked to securities prices through its expectations and behaviour. Consequently, the role of investor sentiment in IPO premiums has received increasing attention. However, existing research has primarily focused on measuring investor sentiment within a single market, with little in-depth exploration from a cross-market perspective. This paper therefore aims to explore the mechanism through which investor sentiment influences IPO premium rates using the DML model. Through empirical analysis, the paper seeks to further understand the role of investor sentiment in IPO premiums, providing a theoretical foundation for the improvement of new stock market systems and the enhancement of market efficiency.
Literature Review
Investor sentiment significantly influences IPO pricing, often leading to over- or under-pricing. Empirical studies consistently show a positive correlation between sentiment and IPO premiums. For instance, Fang Ziyi (2023) [1]used PCA to confirm sentiment’s effect on A+H share premiums, while Xu Yujia (2018) [2] and Ye Yanyan (2014) [3] found that higher sentiment drives up IPO abnormal returns.
The mechanism behind IPO premiums reflects interactions between sentiment, investor structure, and issuance systems. Lü Dongkai and Jiang Xianling (2013) [4]noted that low offering prices and high retail participation increase susceptibility to sentiment. Sun Ziyuan (2009) [5]found underpricing declines with stronger marketization, while Yan Shulian (2012) [6] highlighted inefficiencies from irrational investor behavior. Thus, premiums are shaped by both psychology and institutions.
Measurement methods include text mining, composite indices, and advanced machine learning models. Guo Zhaocheng (2020) [7]quantified sentiment using forum data, while Yan Shulian (2012) [8] and Ye Yanyan (2014) [9] built indices integrating multiple indicators. These tools improve accuracy and provide essential data for sentiment–IPO research.
Finally, sentiment

also affects post-IPO performance. Xie Taifeng and Gao Yi (2016) [10] linked premiums to turnover rates, confidence, and biases in the Growth Enterprise Market. Qin Zhiqiang (2009)[11] observed stronger sentiment effects in small-cap stocks. Regression analyses commonly confirm sentiment as a key driver in behavioral finance explanations of IPO pricing.

III. Theoretical Analysis and Research Hypotheses
A. The direct mechanism of investor sentiment on IPO discount rates
Investor sentiment, as the aggregate manifestation of investors' subjective expectations in capital markets, influences IPO discount rates through cognitive biases in behavioural finance and the game theory logic of market transactions. From the perspective of cognitive biases, Shiller (2003) [12] proposed the theory of ‘irrational exuberance,’ which suggests that during periods of heightened sentiment, investors may overestimate the growth potential of new stocks due to overconfidence or generalise local market heat as a broader trend due to representativeness bias, driving subscription demand to deviate from fundamental support. This irrational demand intensifies subscription competition in the primary market (e.g., declining online subscription rates), forcing underwriters to adopt ‘price suppression compensation’ strategies to attract investors (Rock, 1986) [13], directly leading to an initial deviation between the issue price and the first-day closing price.
From the perspective of transaction game theory, emotion-driven trading behaviour amplifies price volatility in the secondary market. Ljungqvist et al. (2007) [14] found that retail investors are more prone to ‘herd behaviour’ during periods of heightened sentiment, blindly chasing new issues; institutional investors, on the other hand, may exploit sentiment for short-term arbitrage, further reinforcing price deviations. This ‘sentiment-trading’ positive feedback loop causes the first-day closing price to persistently deviate from the issue price, systematically amplifying the positive fluctuations in the discount rate.

B. The logic behind the adjustment effect of issuance scale
As a core supply variable in the IPO market, the scale of issuance has a negative regulatory effect on the relationship between sentiment and discount rates, due to liquidity dilution and optimisation of investor structure. From a liquidity dilution

perspective, Cornelli et al. (2006) [15] proposed the 'liquidity supply hypothesis', which states that large-scale issuance increases the supply of circulating shares, thereby reducing the sensitivity of individual stock prices to sentiment. When the issuance scale expands, the marginal impact of retail investor funds on stock prices is diluted, making it harder for irrational, sentiment-driven transactions to cause concentrated price shocks. For instance, among new shares on the STAR Market with fundraising exceeding 1 billion yuan, a one-standard-deviation increase in sentiment leads to a discount rate that is 30% lower than in smaller-scale issuance groups (Wang Ruting et al., 2022) [16].
From an investor structure perspective, large-scale IPOs typically attract more institutional investors to participate in pricing and allocation. These investors have stronger fundamental analysis capabilities and their enhanced pricing influence helps to mitigate emotional distortions in issue prices (e.g. underwriters must balance the demands of institutional and retail investors). Simultaneously, the long-term holding strategies of institutional investors reduce short-term price volatility, thereby weakening the amplifying effect of emotions on discount rates.
Hypothesis H1: Investor sentiment significantly impacts IPO price suppression rates positively, and this effect is stronger during periods of high sentiment (when the CICSI index is above the sample mean).
Hypothesis H2: The issuance scale negatively moderates the positive relationship between investor sentiment and IPO discount rates, meaning that the larger the issuance scale, the weaker the promotional effect of sentiment on discount rates.
Hypothesis H3: The first-day price fluctuation limit positively moderates the relationship between investor sentiment and IPO discount rates. This means that when a price fluctuation limit exists, the promotional effect of sentiment on discount rates is stronger.
Ⅳ. Research Design
A. The direct mechanism of investor sentiment on IPO discount rates
The aim of this paper is to develop a mechanism that explains the impact of investor sentiment on IPO pricing. While current related studies mostly use traditional OLS regression models for causal inference, such models are limited by endogeneity, measurement error and other factors. For instance, IPO pricing is affected by

various factors, such as company fundamentals, industry trends and underwriter reputation. Omitting these key variables from the model leads to biased estimates of investor sentiment coefficients. Furthermore, high-growth industries may trigger both investor optimism and higher pricing simultaneously, but the OLS regression model cannot distinguish between the independent effects of sentiment and industry. To overcome the limitations of traditional models, many scholars have started to explore the use of machine learning for causal inference (Chernozhukov et al., 2018; Athey et al., 2019; Knittel & Stolper, 2021) [17][18][19], with Double Machine Learning (DML) being a notable approach.
DML, an important method in causal inference, was formally proposed and systematically elaborated by Chernozhukov et al. in 2018. Currently, international academic research on DML primarily follows two major trends: theoretical method innovation and practical application expansion. In terms of application research, this framework has been widely adopted in causal inference studies. For example, Yang's research team (2020) [20] were the first to integrate gradient boosting algorithms into the DML model. They demonstrated through an effect assessment of top accounting firms that DML exhibits superior robustness compared to traditional propensity score matching methods. Another notable study (Zhang et al., 2022) [21] used the natural experiment of the London Night Tube service to evaluate the policy's multidimensional impact on the city's socio-economic landscape. In terms of methodological research, Chiang et al. (2022) [22] proposed an innovative multi-directional cross-fitting estimator to solve the estimation problem of high-dimensional parametric regression and cluster sampling data. The Bodory research group (2022) [23] pioneered the construction of a dynamic analysis framework, achieving accurate measurement of multi-period treatment effects through weighted estimation techniques. By contrast, research in the field of dual machine learning in China is still in its infancy, with existing studies primarily focusing on empirical explorations by Wang Ruting's team (2022) [24] and He Jinan's team (2022) [25] These foundational studies provide important methodological guidance and empirical paradigms for future research. Overall, dual machine learning shows great potential for

theoretical development and practical application. Compared to traditional causal inference models, dual machine learning offers distinct advantages in terms of variable selection and model estimation, rendering it a more suitable approach to address the research questions posed in this paper.
Athey et al. (2019)[26] proposed the Generalized Random Forest (GRF) algorithm as a non-parametric policy evaluation method that effectively mitigates estimation biases commonly encountered in traditional causal inference models, such as propensity score matching and difference-in-differences, which often suffer from high-dimensional covariates, distributional imbalance, or the absence of time-varying structures. GRF significantly enhances the robustness and credibility of policy effect estimation and has been widely applied in various empirical studies (Davis & Heller, 2020[27]; Liu Shenglong et al., 2021[28]). B. Variable settings and selection
 1) Dependent variable: IPO discount rate
 The IPO discount rate is measured using a standard academic metric, expressed as the excess return of the closing price of the new shares on the first trading day relative to the issue price. This indicator directly reflects the deviation between primary market pricing and secondary market performance (Loughran & Ritter, 2004 [29] and serves as a core proxy variable for measuring pricing efficiency. In order to circumvent the impact of extreme values, this paper employs a 1% Winsorisation of the IPO

discount rate and adopts the natural logarithm form to alleviate heteroskedasticity issues.
2) Core explanatory variable: Investor sentiment index
The present paper employs Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to construct a comprehensive sentiment index (SENT), with five dimensional proxy variables selected as the underlying indicators: (1) Market level: The closed-end fund discount rate (CEFD) (2) is indicative of the trading level. The initial day of listing saw a significant increase in turnover rate (Turnover) (3).Issuance level: The Online Lottery Ratio (hereafter referred to as the 'Lottery Ratio') (4)Public opinion level: Sentiment analysis score of the prospectus (based on LSTM text mining) (5)Capital level: The following investigation will examine the scale of frozen funds from new share subscriptions. Following the confirmation of data suitability through the KMO test (>0.7) and the Bartlett's sphericity test (p<0.01), the first principal component (variance contribution rate ≥60%) was extracted as SENT. In order to enhance the robustness of the model, this paper also sets the industry-adjusted value of the Baker-Wurgler Sentiment Index and the average excess return of the industry to which the new share issuance belonged in the 30 days prior to issuance as alternative variables.
3) Control variables
Control variables encompass a set of indicators capturing corporate characteristics and issuance attributes, specifically including: company size, debt-to-equity ratio, return on equity, operating growth, earnings per share, net asset value per share, issue price-to-earnings ratio, and issue size. These variables are categorized into corporate financial traits (e.g., debt-to-equity ratio, return on equity), growth indicators (e.g., operating growth), per-share metrics (e.g., earnings per share, net asset value per share), and issuance characteristics (e.g., issue price-to-earnings ratio, issue size).

In this study, key variables applied in the regression analysis are systematically defined and abbreviated to clarify their roles in exploring IPO - related dynamics. The IPO discount rate, central to measuring pricing deviation, is denoted as IPO (additionally referenced as IPO DR1 to distinguish it among multiple potential measures of IPO discount rates), calculated as ln(closing price on the first day/issue

price), where a higher value signals a greater pricing deviation degree. Serving as the core explanatory variable, the Comprehensive Index of Corporate Investor Sentiment, abbreviated as CICSI, is a composite index integrating economic indicators. It synthesizes news sentiment scores (60% weight), trading turnover rate (20% weight), and financing balance growth rate (20% weight) to gauge investor mood. Among control variables and auxiliary terms, the Constant (abbreviated as Constant) acts as the intercept in regression models, capturing baseline effects; Observations (shortened to Obs) represent the total sample count; Control variable terms (CV Terms) encapsulate a set of control variables (e.g., company - specific traits like size) to isolate core factor impacts; Control variable quadratic term (CV QT) accounts for potential non - linear relationships between control variables and the explained variable; and Industry fixed effects (Ind FE) control for unobserved, time - invariant industry - specific characteristics (e.g., industry norms), with all these elements collectively facilitating a nuanced analysis of IPO pricing and related market patterns, whose specific functions will be further detailed in subsequent sections.C. The IPO data for the listed companies under scrutiny in this paper is sourced from two databases: the Wind Database (Wind) and the Guotai An Database (CSMAR). Investor sentiment data is derived from the monthly CICSI index, constructed using unstructured data such as news sentiment analysis and stock forum sentiment. The data is then subjected to a further filtration process, which excludes financial listed companies; IPOs where the interval between the issuance date and the first trading day exceeds five days; and ST/*ST companies and samples with missing data. Continuous variables were subjected to two-sided 1% percentile Winsorisation. Right-skewed variables, such as IPO discount rates, were transformed using natural logarithms to satisfy the normality assumption. In instances where financial data was not available, the study team manually completed or excluded the data from the annual reports of the listed companies. In instances where components of sentiment indicators were not available, this study utilised linear interpolation as a methodology to address the absence of data.

Furthermore, standardisation was performed. Prior to conducting the principal component analysis, the emotional proxy variables were standardised using the Z-score method. C. Analysis of adjustment mechanisms
The present study introduces the concept of issuance scale as a moderating variable and finds that the interaction term coefficient between investor sentiment and issuance scale is significantly negative at the 10% level. This finding indicates that an increase in issuance scale significantly suppresses the positive impact of investor sentiment on IPO discount rates. The results of the study are presented in Table V. This finding lends support to the liquidity supply hypothesis, which posits that IPOs with larger issuance scales have the capacity to attract a greater number of rational institutional investors. This, in turn, has the effect of offsetting the impact of retail investors' emotional trading through increased market liquidity and pricing efficiency. This finding provides new evidence for understanding the IPO pricing mechanism in China's capital market and offers empirical support for the policy direction of 'increasing the proportion of new share issuance' in the current registration system reform. The findings suggest that expanding issuance size may be an effective way to suppress excessive market sentiment reactions.

D.Heterogeneity analysis
As shown in Figure II, the feature importance analysis indicates that among the various factors affecting IPO underpricing, issuance size stands out with a feature importance value of 0.72, far exceeding that of other variables. This suggests that issuance size plays a dominant role in IPO pricing efficiency. The result is consistent with market practice: larger issuance sizes are often associated with liquidity dilution and

optimization of investor structure, thereby significantly influencing the degree of underpricing.
In contrast, the importance of issuance P/E ratio and earnings per share is considerably lower, at 0.09 and 0.04, respectively, indicating that their marginal contribution to model interpretation is limited. This implies that in the subsequent steps of heterogeneity analysis, issuance size may be treated as a core moderating variable to further examine its interaction with investor sentiment in shaping IPO underpricing, while also verifying whether market conditions and profitability exhibit stronger moderating effects under specific circumstances.

As shown in Figure V, the moderating effect of earnings per share (EPS) on the relationship between investor sentiment and IPO underpricing exhibits certain volatility and nonlinear characteristics. First, when EPS is negative or at a relatively low level, the Conditional Average Treatment Effect (CATE) remains relatively high and shows an upward trend. This indicates that when firms have weak profitability or are in a loss-making position, investors rely more heavily on market sentiment, thereby amplifying the role of sentiment in the pricing process.
Second, when EPS is close to zero, the CATE drops sharply to its lowest point, suggesting that at the break-even threshold, the market tends to rely more on

This implies that while sentiment continues to exert a positive effect on IPO pricing as profitability improves, its strength is weaker compared to firms with low earnings, reflecting an enhanced role of rational market behavior.
Overall, EPS exerts a nonlinear moderating effect on the sentiment–IPO underpricing relationship: firms with low profitability or losses are more easily driven by sentiment, whereas firms with stronger profitability remain influenced by sentiment, but to a lesser extent. This finding reveals the interaction mechanism between firm fundamentals and market sentiment, emphasizing the important heterogeneous role of profitability in IPO pricing efficiency.

VI. Empirical results analysis
The phenomenon of IPO underpricing is prevalent in global capital markets and is particularly pronounced in China’s A-share market, continuously attracting considerable attention from both academia and industry. Traditional financial theories fail to fully account for this phenomenon, while behavioral finance perspectives suggest that investor sentiment may play a critical role in influencing IPO pricing efficiency. Against this backdrop, this study employs investor sentiment data and IPO underpricing data from China’s A-share market between 2019 and 2023, utilizing Double Machine Learning (DML) and Generalized Random Forests (GRF) to systematically examine the impact of investor sentiment on IPO pricing efficiency. Furthermore, the study investigates the heterogeneity of issuance size, issuance P/E ratio, and earnings per share (EPS).
The empirical results demonstrate that investor sentiment has a significant positive effect on IPO underpricing, and this conclusion remains robust after controlling for endogeneity and conducting multiple robustness checks. Further analysis reveals that firm-specific characteristics exert heterogeneous moderating effects on the relationship between sentiment and IPO pricing efficiency. Specifically, issuance size plays a pivotal differentiating role: smaller offerings are more susceptible to sentiment fluctuations, while larger issues exhibit stronger

stability and more rational pricing. Similarly, issuance P/E ratio displays an inverted-U moderating effect—sentiment exerts limited influence at both low and high valuation levels but reaches its peak at moderate levels, indicating the strongest sentiment-driven impact. Earnings per share also reflects a nonlinear moderating pattern: firms with weak profitability or in loss-making positions are more sentiment-driven, whereas highly profitable firms remain influenced by sentiment to a lesser extent.
Based on these findings, this paper proposes the following policy recommendations:
First, increase the proportion of new share issuance and expand issuance scale. The core objective is to establish a flexible issuance mechanism that dynamically adjusts supply according to market conditions, thereby meeting the financing needs of high-quality enterprises while maintaining supply-demand balance. Implementation should particularly support technology innovation and strategic emerging industries, accompanied by the improvement of market-oriented pricing mechanisms and stabilization tools, as well as necessary buffer measures and investor protection systems to preserve both vitality and stability in the market.
Second, design differentiated trading mechanisms for new shares. Regulators may categorize listed firms into growth, mature, and special types according to firm characteristics and risk profiles, and apply differentiated price fluctuation limits accordingly: wider ranges for growth firms to strengthen price discovery, stable limits for mature firms, and transitional arrangements for special firms. In addition, liquidity adjustment factors and circuit breakers should be introduced, along with reinforced market-making responsibilities, enhanced investor suitability management, and stricter disclosure requirements, thereby improving pricing efficiency while containing risks.
Third, strengthen the monitoring of abnormal trading activities. Establish intelligent real-time monitoring systems to detect behaviors such as frequent cancellations and abnormal volatility, and implement tiered supervision with watchlists for high-frequency accounts. A comprehensive framework for the identification and management of abnormal transactions should be developed, with manipulative behaviors placed under priority supervision. By promoting cross-agency data sharing and fast-response

mechanisms, regulatory effectiveness can be enhanced to balance market dynamism with risk prevention, thereby fostering the healthy development of the IPO market.

 Regarding 2025 US ”Reciprocal Tariffs” policy that significantly raises average tariffs on major
trading partners and reshapes global trade cost structure, this paper constructs multi-layer quanti-
tative assessment frameworks across soybeans, automobiles, semiconductors, tariff revenue, and
macroeconomic manufacturing reshoring to evaluate impacts on US domestic industry .
 For Problem 1, given China’s differentiated preferences for soybean sources, we construct Arm-
ington demand model to characterize China’s soybean import structure by source, combined with
structural gravity and supply response models to describe global trade and production adjustments.
Results show: as tariffs on US soybeans increase from 3% to 13%-25%, US export volume and
value to China drop from 50% to 16%-26%, while Brazil and Argentina substantially increase
market share through expansion and price adjustment, largely filling China’s import gap.
 For Problem 2, considering Japanese automakers’ multi-location production (Japan, Mexico,
US) and tariff response capabilities, we establish multi-production-path cost-minimization and nested
Logit demand models linked with structural gravity and input-output frameworks to characterize
trade and industry transmission. Results show: increased tariffs on Japanese vehicles shift pro-
duction from Japan toward Mexico and US, boosting US and North American auto value-added and
employment to some degree, yet average vehicle prices rise two percentage points, and import share
declines noticeably.
 For Problem 3, we construct multi-stage global semiconductor supply chain network flow
model incorporating downstream demand and dynamic capacity evolution equations, simulating
chip manufacturing layout and trade flows under various tariff and export control combinations.
Results show: high tariffs partially replacing subsidies significantly raise US mid-high-end pro-
cess capacity and domestic manufacturing share, yet require higher fiscal and downstream costs;
global supply chain concentration rises with increased dependence on allied regions, reflecting clear
efficiency-security tradeoffs.
 For Problem 4, from HS item level we construct partial-equilibrium tariff revenue model with
structural gravity trade-shift module and dynamic Laffer-effect adjustment model. Results show:
reciprocal tariffs initially boost revenue substantially (exceeding 40% in some years), but with trade
contraction and partner retaliation, cumulative four-year revenue gains are limited, even falling be-
low baseline in some scenarios.
 For Problem 5, we construct multi-sector dynamic input-output and trade shock model com-
bined with manufacturing reshoring decisions and Manufacturing Reshoring Index (MRI), embed-
ding simplified financial market shock module to transmit tariffs and countermeasures through US
agriculture, manufacturing, services, and finance. Results show: high tariffs and countermeasures
modestly raise US manufacturing capacity and MRI, yet increase prices, compress external demand,
suppress investment; GDP and employment gains are limited and unsustainable; actual manufactur-
ing ”reshoring” magnitude is moderate, far from policy-claimed ”large-scale reshoring.”

 I. Problem Restatement

1 . 1 Problem Background
 April 2025: US government announces ”Reciprocal Tariffs” policy imposing minimum 10%
baseline tariffs on all trading partners, with additional 11%-50% tariffs on 60 countries with large
US trade deficits. Under this backdrop, global trade patterns and supply chains face reshaping:
agricultural trade (e.g., soybeans) shows clear shifts; Japanese automakers pursue tariff avoidance
through ”localization + third-country layout”; semiconductor industry faces heightened supply chain
security and tech competition risks amid combined tariffs, subsidies and export controls; US tariff
revenue surges short-term, but long-term impacts of import cost increases, trade contraction and
alliance shifts remain unclear.

1 . 2 Problem Requirements
 Problem 1: Soybean trade patterns and tariff impacts. Model soybean export volumes, val-
ues and market share redistribution among US, China, Brazil and Argentina following US reciprocal
tariffs and countermeasures.
 Problem 2: US-Japan auto trade and non-tariff responses. Analyze Japan’s market posi-
tion, non-tariff responses and economic transmission mechanisms; assess changes in US-Japan auto
trade, US import structure, and US domestic auto industry from increased Japanese car tariffs.
 Problem 3: Semiconductor industry security and tariff policy. Model different chip grades’
trade and production amid combined tariffs, subsidies and high-end export controls; analyze tariff
impacts on US domestic manufacturing capacity, industry profits and supply chain security.
 Problem 4: Dynamic tariff revenue changes and second-term forecasts. Build HS-level
dynamic model of tariff revenue and trade volume; assess tariff revenue paths and ranges during
Trump’s second term, considering trade elasticity and policy uncertainty.
 Problem 5: Macroeconomic comprehensive effects and manufacturing reshoring assess-
ment. Build comprehensive model capturing sectoral output, employment, trade balances and fi-
nancial market fluctuations; assess whether reciprocal tariffs actually promote US manufacturing
reshoring short-to-medium term and whether macro costs are acceptable.

 From demand-side using Armington import structure model for China’s soybean consumption
shares from different sources; from supply-side using structural gravity and simplified supply re-
sponse models to estimate tariff-scenario trade redistribution among US, Brazil, Argentina.

tariffs, shipping, exchange rates and non-tariff costs, combined with input-output analysis, charac-

(1) Armington Model: US-China Soybean Trade Restructuring

 Armington model (Figure 2) shows: as China’s tariffs escalate from moderate to heavy retali-

remains stable, but import structure shifts from ”US-centered” to ”Brazil-centered with Argentina
as supplement,” showing typical tariff-driven trade diversion rather than contraction.

(2) Structural Gravity Model: Alternative Tariff Elasticity Characterization

 Abstract
 Against the backdrop of accelerating global digitalization and mounting climate pressures,
 enabling digital-economy growth while simultaneously controlling carbon emissions has
 become a critical challenge for China. This study constructs a Digital Economy Devel-
 opment Index (DEI) and a Carbon Emissions Index (CEI) to examine the spatiotemporal
 evolution and spatial heterogeneity of coordinated development between the digital econ-
 omy and carbon emissions. We employ global and local Moran’s I, a spatial Markov chain
 model, and kernel density estimation to investigate spatiotemporal autocorrelation, interre-
 gional transition patterns, and the dynamic evolution of the coupling coordination degree
 over 2011–2022. The results indicate that China’s eastern region performs notably better in
 achieving coordinated development, maintaining persistently higher coupling coordination
 levels. In contrast, the central and western regions face substantial challenges; in particular,
 low-value areas exhibit considerable potential to transition toward higher-value states,
 suggesting substantial room for improvement. The spatiotemporal analysis further reveals
 pronounced regional disparities and provides a scientific basis for policymaking aimed at
 advancing green and low-carbon development strategies tailored to regional characteristics.

 Keywords: coupling coordination degree; digital economy development index; carbon
 emissions index; spatiotemporal evolution

 According to the consensus reached at the 26th UN Climate Change Conference (COP26),
 global carbon emissions must decline substantially over the coming decades to curb the
 adverse impacts of climate change [6]. As one of the world’s largest carbon emitters, China
 faces intense pressure to control carbon emissions while simultaneously advancing the
 rapid development of its digital economy [7]. In response, the Chinese government has
 articulated the “dual-carbon” targets—peaking carbon emissions before 2030 and achieving
 carbon neutrality before 2060 [8]. Achieving these targets requires not only accelerating
 industrial restructuring and improving energy efficiency but also addressing the tensions
 between digital-economy development and carbon-emissions control. In this context, a
 key scientific and policy question is whether digital-economy development and carbon-
 emissions control can evolve in a coordinated manner across regions with substantial
 heterogeneity in China [9]. Therefore, enabling sustained growth of the digital economy
 while effectively curbing carbon emissions [10] and promoting regionally differentiated
 green and low-carbon transitions [11] have become urgent issues in China’s development
 agenda. Accordingly, it is necessary to evaluate the coupling and coordination between the
 digital economy and carbon emissions from a spatiotemporal perspective, especially given
 China’s pronounced regional heterogeneity.
 Most existing studies have provided preliminary evidence on the nexus between the
 digital economy and carbon emissions, mainly examining whether digital-economy devel-
 opment can facilitate emissions reduction [12], enhance resource-use efficiency through
 digital technologies [13], and optimize the energy structure [14]. The related research also
 explores carbon mitigation and spatiotemporal carbon assessments from ecological and
 land-use perspectives, such as CO2 emission compensation by urban green spaces [15]
 and land-use carbon budget and carbon balance capacity analyses [16]. However, the
 current literature is largely constrained to qualitative discussions or analyses based on a
 single dimension [17]. In particular, three limitations deserve further attention. First, many
 studies focus on one-directional effects (e.g., whether digitalization reduces emissions) and
 pay insufficient attention to whether digital-economy development and carbon-emissions
 control can progress in a coordinated manner over time [18]. Second, although China
 exhibits pronounced regional disparities, the existing studies have not fully captured
 the spatial dependence and spatiotemporal heterogeneity of digitalization and carbon
 emissions across regions, which may lead to incomplete policy implications [19]. Third,
 provinces differ substantially in carbon-emissions growth [20], emission levels, and mitiga-
 tion potential [21]; these differences are closely related to local economic foundations [22],
 industrial structures [23], energy-consumption patterns [24], and policy environments [23],
 implying that the digital economy–carbon nexus may evolve unevenly across space.
 Accordingly, this study investigates the spatiotemporal evolution of the coupling
 coordination between China’s digital economy and carbon emissions from a regional
 heterogeneity perspective. We first establish comprehensive evaluation index systems for
 the Digital Economy Development Index (DEI) and the Carbon Emissions Index (CEI) and
 compute the two indices based on provincial data [25,26]. To improve the robustness of
 the index construction under non-normal data characteristics, we determine the indicator
 weights by integrating the CRITIC–Spearman method with the entropy weight method
 (EWM) [27]. We then measure the coupling coordination degree (CCD) between DEI and
 CEI to evaluate their coordinated development across provinces. Next, global and local
 Moran’s I are employed to examine the spatial autocorrelation and clustering patterns of
 CCD [24]. Based on the local Moran’s I classification, we further construct a spatial Markov
 chain model to reveal CCD state transitions under different spatial-lag contexts and to
 characterize the neighborhood-conditioned evolution process [28]. In addition, kernel

 3. Results
 In this study, we begin by computing the Digital Economy Development Index (DEI)
 and the Carbon Emissions Index (CEI). These indices allow us to examine the temporal
 trends of digital economy development and carbon emissions. Next, we calculate the cou-
 pling coordination degree (CCD) between DEI and CEI and assess the spatial dependence
 across provinces using global Moran’s I and local Moran’s I. A spatial contiguity matrix
 (adjacency matrix) is specified as the spatial weight matrix for this analysis.
 Building on the results from the local Moran’s I classification, we then apply a spatial
 Markov chain model to reveal the evolutionary patterns of CCD over time and across spatial
 units. Finally, using kernel density estimation (KDE), we visualize the spatiotemporal
 distribution of the coupling coordination degree. This helps to illustrate how the density of
 CCD changes over both years and regions.

 3.1. Measurement Results of the Two Indices (DEI and CEI)
 Based on the data shown in Figure 2 for the period 2011–2022, the provincial trajec-
 tories of the Digital Economy Development Index (DEI) and the Carbon Emissions Index
 (CEI) exhibit pronounced heterogeneity. To present the temporal evolution in a clear and
 representative manner, we report the local Moran’s I maps for 2011, 2016, and 2022, which
 correspond to the beginning, middle, and end of the study period, thereby providing
 an intuitive snapshot of the early-stage pattern, mid-period adjustment, and end-period
 configuration of spatial association.
 Overall, the DEI increased in most provinces, with particularly strong and sustained
 growth in the eastern and coastal regions, such as Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang.
 These provinces maintained relatively high DEI levels and continued to improve over
 time, reflecting ongoing upgrades in digital infrastructure and digitalization. Notably,
 Beijing’s DEI rose from 0.25 in 2011 to 0.74 in 2022, highlighting the rapid expansion of the
 digital economy.
 In contrast, the pattern for CEI shows that carbon-emission pressures remain signifi-
 cant in certain regions, especially in western provinces like Inner Mongolia and Xinjiang,
 where the CEI values remain relatively high. This suggests that these regions continue to
 face substantial challenges in emission mitigation. Despite progress in digital-economy
 development, carbon-emission constraints in these areas remain binding.
 In contrast, the CEI results suggest that carbon-emission pressure has intensified in
 some resource- and energy-intensive provinces, such as Inner Mongolia, Ningxia, and
 Xinjiang. Specifically, the CEI values in these regions show a declining trend, which
 indicates worsening carbon-emission conditions and increasing mitigation pressure.

 4.2. Regional Disparities and Evolution of CCD
 The results point to a persistent east–central–west gradient in coupling coordination,
 but the nature of this disparity is not simply a static ranking. At the level of long-run
 averages, provinces in the eastern region remain clustered at higher CCD values, which
 is consistent with the spatial autocorrelation patterns reported in Table 4 and Figure 5.
 Importantly, this regional dominance is accompanied by stronger “high-level lock-in”: once
 provinces reach upper-middle or high coordination states, the spatial Markov matrices
 show high probabilities of remaining there, particularly under H–H neighborhood contexts.
 In other words, the eastern region’s advantage is not only reflected in higher levels but
 also in stronger stability and persistence of coordination states. This persistence helps
 explain why regional differences can remain visible even when all provinces are improving,
 because provinces located within high-level clusters tend to reinforce each other through
 stable neighborhood regimes rather than frequently switching states.
 Meanwhile, the evolution pattern highlights a more meaningful dynamic on the
 “catching-up” side. The central and western regions show a clearer rightward shift in the
 distribution over time, as illustrated by the heterogeneity trajectories in Figure 7 and the
 distributional change in Figure 6. This shift is not merely a uniform upward movement but
 is associated with more frequent transitions from lower states to middle states, especially
 under L–L and L–H neighborhood types. The spatial Markov heterogeneity results further
 indicate that upward mobility becomes more visible in later subperiods, implying that
 coordination improvement in lagging regions follows a gradual accumulation path rather
 than a sudden leap. Taken together, the evidence supports a two-layer interpretation of
 regional evolution: the eastern region largely reflects high-level stability with moderate
 incremental changes, whereas the central and western regions contribute more to the
 overall “movement of the distribution” through stronger upgrading momentum, which
 gradually narrows the coordination gap while leaving the spatial structure broadly intact.

 adjacency-only neighborhood definitions. Third, the interval-perturbation test on the CCD
 state thresholds produces transition matrices that are highly similar to the baseline results,
 which implies that the persistence and upgrading structure captured by the spatial Markov
 chain is not sensitive to minor shifts in classification cutoffs. Taken together, these results
 strengthen confidence that the reported clustering, persistence, and regional upgrading
 tendencies reflect structural spatial regularities rather than parameter or specification noise.
 At the same time, the interpretation of the CCD requires clear boundaries. The CCD is a
 synthetic measure that summarizes the joint configuration of digital-economy development
 and carbon-emissions performance, rather than a causal estimate of digitalization’s impact
 on emissions. A high CCD can emerge either because a province achieves simultaneous
 improvement in both subsystems, or because one subsystem advances faster while the
 other improves more slowly but remains consistent in direction. This implies that the
 CCD should be used primarily as a diagnostic indicator for regional coordination status
 and its spatial evolution, instead of being read as direct evidence of emission-reduction
 effects. From a policy perspective, the spatial persistence observed in high-level clusters
 suggests that provinces with strong digital foundations may benefit most from deepening
 green digital applications such as industrial upgrading, energy-system management, and
 data-driven efficiency improvements, to consolidate coordination advantages. For the
 central and western regions, where upgrading momentum is visible, but the initial levels
 remain lower, policies may need to focus on reducing structural constraints that hinder joint
 progress, including the reliance on carbon-intensive production, weaker green technology
 diffusion, and limited spillover channels. In this sense, coordinated development is likely
 to be strengthened not only through local digital investment but also through cross-regional
 linkages that allow latecomers to access cleaner technologies, digital governance capacity,
 and low-carbon industrial pathways.

 5. Conclusions
 This study analyzes the coupling coordination degree between the DEI and the CEI
 across 30 provincial-level regions in China, revealing pronounced spatial and temporal
 heterogeneity in the digital economy–carbon emissions nexus. In the eastern region, the
 coupling coordination degree exhibits a marked upward trend, especially during 2015–
 2022, indicating strong synergistic capacity and a progressive strengthening of coordination
 between digital-economy development and carbon-mitigation efforts. The central region
 shows a relatively steady increase with limited fluctuations, suggesting that coordination
 challenges persist, particularly in aligning digitalization with emissions control. The west-
 ern region remains at a comparatively low coordination level, yet it also demonstrates
 gradual improvement, implying that under policy support and enhanced regional co-
 ordination, the synergy between digital-economy development and carbon emissions is
 steadily strengthening.
 Further evidence indicates that the coupling coordination increases over time across
 regions, with particularly notable upward mobility in low and lower-middle areas, reflect-
 ing substantial transformation potential and room for improvement. The results from the
 spatial Markov chain analysis show strong persistence among high-value provinces in
 the eastern region, whereas provinces in the central and western regions exhibit higher
 upward transition potential, offering important implications for future policy design.
 Overall, the findings underscore significant regional disparities in coordinated devel-
 opment between the digital economy and carbon emissions in China, highlighting the
 need for region-differentiated policy interventions tailored to local conditions to advance
 sustainable development.

数字经济对区域绿色全要素生产率影响的实证分析
——基于中国省际面板数据的视角
摘要
在过去40多年里，我国借助改革开放及全球化浪潮实现了经济的快速增长。但传统上依赖重工业和基础设施建设的模式也带来了环境污染和排放问题。党的二十大报告突出了实现经济社会全面绿色转型的必要性，旨在促进人与自然的和谐共存。面对科技革命和产业变革的新机遇，数字经济作为一项战略选择，能够提升资源使用效率并促进可再生能源的开发利用，对于中国经济的绿色转型具有关键作用。因此，探究数字经济发展对绿色发展的影响对于中国当前阶段的高质量发展具有重要意义。
本研究基于2014至2022年中国30个省、直辖市、自治区的面板数据，深入探讨了数字经济对区域绿色发展的影响。研究首先明确了研究背景、问题、思路和方法，然后利用熵值法和SBM-DEA模型的GML生产率指数，构建了数字经济发展水平指标体系，并测度了各省的绿色发展水平。研究发现，数字经济显著正向影响区域绿色发展，即使在考虑内生性和控制变量后，这一影响仍然稳健。此外，数字经济对东部地区的绿色发展促进作用更为显著，而对中西部地区的影响不显著，反映了区域间的异质性。
进一步地，研究使用系统GMM模型分析了数字经济发展对绿色发展的动态效应，发现绿色发展具有内生继承性，数字经济的正向影响在动态过程中持续显著。空间杜宾模型分析揭示了数字经济对绿色发展的空间效应，即一个地区的绿色发展不仅受本地区数字经济影响，还受到邻近地区的正向溢出效应。门槛效应检验表明，科技创新水平是影响数字经济与绿色发展关系的一个重要门槛变量，当科技创新水平较高时，数字经济对绿色发展的正向推动作用更为显著。
根据上述分析结果，文章提出了以下建议：政府应加大对西部地区数字化基础设施的资金投入和技术支持，以促进区域间的平衡发展；应重视科技创新能力的培养，加强人才引进与培养，提升自主创新能力，以充分发挥数字经济对绿色发展的推动作用。利用数字化技术和手段实现产品的环保标识和监管，优化数据中心能效，推动数字经济的可持续发展。
关键字：数字经济；绿色发展；空间效应；门槛检验

一、引言
（一）研究背景
自1978年改革开放以来，中国经济总量显著增长，从3645亿元增至2021年的126万亿元，对全球经济增长贡献达32%。但这种增长伴随着能源消耗、环境污染和资源枯竭等问题，以及要素禀赋趋紧、劳动力红利减少和资本收益降低等挑战。因此，实现经济增长与生态环境保护的绿色发展是中国经济发展的必然选择。
数字经济作为新兴经济形态，是中国未来发展的新动力。当前，中国正处于转型发展的关键时期，提升国家效率和经济质量，特别是生态文明建设，是重点任务。在科技革命和产业变革的背景下，推动数字经济的快速发展，优化资源配置，是实现经济模式转型的关键。通过数字经济赋能传统产业，促进产业升级和绿色发展，将为中国的生态文明建设和经济高质量发展提供重要支撑。 REF _Ref165315033 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [1] 
（二）研究目的与意义
1.研究目的
基于上述背景，本研究将详细探讨区域数字经济和绿色发展的现状，深入分析它们的发展态势和主要特点。通过深入分析两者之间的关系，我们旨在明确数字经济对绿色发展的影响效果及其作用机制，展现数字经济发展在推动区域绿色增长方面的潜力，为数字经济更有效地促进绿色发展提供有益的见解和参考。
2.研究意义
“我们既要绿水青山，也要金山银山。宁要绿水青山，不要金山银山，而且绿水青山就是金山银山。”习总书记的“两山”理论蕴含的以人为本、和谐共生、责任担当等价值理念是生态文明建设的重要价值遵循。而数字经济，作为21世纪中国推动重大战略转型的新引擎，正站在新一轮科技革命的前沿，把握由此带来的历史性发展机遇。通过积极发展数字经济，中国旨在为绿色发展注入持续而强大的动力，以科技创新为核心推动力，促进经济结构的优化升级和增长方式的根本转变。本文在深入总结中国数字经济进程中所呈现的绿色发展的典型特征与客观规律的基础上，探究数字经济对绿色发展所产生的影响效应以及背后的作用机制，其对于促进经济的绿色高质量增长不仅具有重要的理论价值，也具备显著的现实意义。
（1）理论意义：本文在国内外相关文献研究的基础上，结合区域统计数据，使用数字经济测度指标体系和绿色全要素生产率分别概括我国在四大板块的数字经济和绿色发展的情况，建立了数字经济对绿色发展影响的分析框架；同时，对数字经济赋能绿色发展进行机制分析。该研究可以为实现数字经济推进区域绿色发展的过程中出现的问题提供一定的理论依据，因此具有重要的理论意义。
（2）现实意义：本研究全面评估了中国30个省份数字经济和绿色发展的现状，特别是对区域间的差异性进行了深入分析，这有助于各地区科学地、动态地利用绿色经济来驱动绿色发展。此外，文章还深入探讨了数字经济与绿色发展的协同发展途径和具体实施策略，对于推动中国经济实现数字化与绿色化的双重转型具有重要的现实意义。
（三）研究内容与创新点
1.研究内容

本文聚焦于区域绿色发展，并从中国数字经济发展水平的角度出发，探讨二者之间的联系。第一部分，主要介绍了数字经济与绿色发展的背景，阐述了本文的主要研究目的、内容以及创新点；第二部分，则通过文献综述法，对国内外关于数字经济、绿色发展以及数字经济对绿色发展影响的相关研究进行了概述；第三部分主要介绍了数据来源、指标测度与模型解释：本文采用2014-2022年的省级面板数据进行了数字经济发展水平指标构建。同时基于SBM-DEA模型的GML生产率指数测算了各省的绿色发展水平。最后介绍了数据的选取与来源以及各个模型的构建；第四部分着重于模型的建立和分析：首先对区域数字经济发展水平和区域绿色发展水平进行了评价，建立了二者间的统计关系。接着依次通过基准回归、内生性检验、稳健性检验、区域异质性分析系统研究了数字经济发展水平与区域绿色发展的影响关系。最后进一步做了空间效应分析与门槛检验，具体分析了数字经济怎样影响区域绿色发展；第五部分研究结论与建议。总结了研究发现，并根据分析结果，就如何更有效地利用数字经济推动绿色发展提出了具体建议。
2.研究创新点
第一，本文站在新的研究视角上进行研究。文章立足于“双碳”目标背景下，以新发展理念为理论指导，将焦点从传统经济增长转向了绿色发展水平的探讨。同时，随着中国数字经济的不断成熟，其以慢慢深入到了各个行业，文章针对数字经济发展水平对区域绿色发展的影响进行了研究，这结合了当前的热点议题，提供了一个较为新颖的研究视角。
第二，文章在详细探讨了数字经济如何影响绿色发展的具体路径后，进一步剖析了数字经济促进绿色发展的内在作用机制。鉴于中国当前面临的严峻环境挑战和产业结构的不平衡状况，研究数字经济对绿色发展水平提升的作用及其作用机制具有重要意义。文章还利用空间滞后模型，探讨了数字经济对区域绿色发展的潜在空间效应及其随地理距离变化的规律，为数字经济与绿色经济效率领域的研究提供了新的视角和深入理解。
第三，基于SBM-DEA的GML生产率指数来测度我国各省的绿色发展水平，传统的DEA模型在处理多投入或少产出情况时存在局限，而超效率SBM模型解决了这一问题，并且在构建指标体系时更紧密地贴合了绿色发展的概念，综合地考虑了资源和能源投入要素。
二、文献综述
（一）数字经济相关研究
数字经济，作为现代经济发展的一股新兴力量，以其迅猛的发展速度、广泛的辐射范围和深远的影响程度，正在引领生产方式、生活方式和治理方式的深刻变革。它不仅重塑了全球要素资源的配置，而且重新定义了全球经济结构，更在改变全球竞争格局中扮演着关键角色。国内外相关学者不断对其进行深入研究，数字经济的定义、影响以及测度等方面都有了较为清晰、系统的研究。 REF _Ref165315141 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [2]
1.数字经济概念研究
数字经济的概念最早于1996年由“数字经济之父”Tapscott REF _Ref165315155 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [3]在其著作《数字经济》中提出数字经济是以互联网发展为基础的智能时代，并通过智能化来推动经济社会进步。随后世界各国学者皆陆续投入了相关研究，Kim et al.（2002） REF _Ref165315166 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [4]将数字经济定义为一种新的经济发展范式，主要包括数字化交易的商品与服务；赵涛（2020） REF _Ref165315242 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [5]指出数字经济具有促进生产链产业链数字化转型的特点。G20 杭州峰会 REF _Ref165315253 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [6]也对数字经济做出清晰定义：数字经济是指将数字化知识和信息作为关键生产要素、以现代信息网络作为重要载体、以信息通信技术的有效使用作为效率提升和经济结构优化的重要推动力的一系列经济活动。此定义突出了数字技术、数据要素等核心内容，且具有一定系统性，受到较多学者认可。
2.数字经济影响效应研究
数字经济作为一种新兴现象，对经济社会产生的影响具有双重性。Asongu S（2020） REF _Ref165315283 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [7]基于发展不平衡视角，通过对163个国家的实证分析发现，在数字化普及方面，发展中国家比发达国家享有更大的收益，它们可以利用数字经济的后发优势来减少与发达国家之间的差距。夏杰长等（2021） REF _Ref165315295 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [8]则聚焦于区域创新，实证研究表明数字经济能增加区域创新的投资，进而提高区域创新产出。同时，钟春平（2020） REF _Ref165315304 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [9]在研究数字经济的创造性破坏效应时指出，这种破坏效应导致社会资源的重新分配，可能引起失业、焦虑等社会问题。这些研究揭示了数字经济发展的多维影响，既有积极的增长和创新潜力，也伴随着潜在的社会挑战。
3.数字经济测算研究
在数字经济的测算方面，学者们普遍采用构建综合指标评价体系的方法来衡量数字经济发展水平。刘军等（2020） REF _Ref165315384 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [10]、王娟娟等（2021） REF _Ref165315416 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [11]、王军等（2021） REF _Ref165315421 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [12]研究者分别从不同的角度出发，建立了省级层面的数字经济发展评价指标体系，从而对我国各省份的数字经济发展水平进行了客观评估。赵涛等（2020） REF

_Ref165315450 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [13]则首次提出了以城市互联网发展水平和数字金融发展为两个主要维度的中国城市层面数字经济发展评价指标体系，测度出各城市的数字经济综合发展指数，为城市层面数字经济的研究奠定了良好基础。
（二）绿色发展相关研究
遵循绿色发展之路能够有效解决我国经济发展与环境保护、资源约束间的矛盾问题，推动我国经济实现高质量发展。随着绿色发展政策实践持续落地的同时，学术界绿色研究也愈发深入。
1.绿色发展定义研究
世界银行和国务院发展研究中心联合课题组 REF _Ref165315478 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [14]在2013年关注经济与生态发展的平衡性，定义绿色发展为不过度依赖资源使用与牺牲环境的经济增长方式，这种增长通过建立绿色产品市场、创新绿色技术、发展绿色投资和推广绿色消费等手段实现。王海芹和高世楫（2016） REF _Ref165315494 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [15]则基于目的论定义绿色发展，认为其是追求高效、全面、可持续的经济发展，目标是实现绿色富国、绿色惠民。周小亮（2020） REF _Ref165315503 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [16]从绿色发展的意义角度定义绿色发展，认为其是实现经济增长、生态环境及社会公平相协调的发展方向和重要途径，能够推动经济社会实现高质量发展。
2.绿色发展影响因素研究
近年来，全球对环境保护和气候变化问题的关注度日益增加，绿色发展成为中国实现未来可持续性发展的核心政策。综合审视影响绿色发展的相关文献，可以发现影响绿色发展的主要因素大致包括五个方面：产业结构的升级与转型、技术创新的水平、城市发展的方式、制度的安排以及绿色金融的发展状况。陈超凡（2016） REF _Ref165315503 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [17]的研究进一步证实了能源结构对于工业绿色要素生产率具有正相关性，表明通过调整能源结构可以有效促进工业部门的绿色增长。Acemoglu等学者（2020） REF _Ref165315581 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [18]提出，将排污收费和环保补助相结合的策略能以最高效率推进绿色技术的应用以及节能减排的实践。张建鹏等人（2021） REF _Ref165315585 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [19]则系统地梳理了环境政策和金融发展如何共同作用于绿色经济转型的过程。
3.绿色发展测算研究
在探究绿色发展的衡量方法方面，学术界已经展开了大量研究并建立了各种指标体系。明翠琴（2016） REF _Ref165315610 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [20]针对中国特定行业，如渔业，探讨了其对国家经济绿色增长的贡献，并为此设计了一套评价指标体系。另一方面，崔元锋（2009） REF _Ref165315636 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [21]等学者通过构建一个包含66项指标的模型，对中国30个省（区、市）在2009年的绿色发展水平进行了详尽分析。此外，王开科等人（2020） REF _Ref165315650 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [22]也从经济、社会和环境三个维度出发，利用数十个统计变量来构建了一个综合的绿色发展评价指标体系。
（三）数字经济对绿色发展影响相关研究
目前围绕数字经济与绿色发展相关研究日益丰富，但大多聚焦于宏观层面，其中主要探讨数字经济对区域城市碳排放、污染排放等的影响及其具体作用机制。Grossman 和Krueger（1995） REF _Ref165315664 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [23]指出经济增长对生态环境产生影响主要是通过规模效应、技术效应与结构效应得以实现。Lange S等（2020） REF _Ref165315673 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [24]则更进一步指出数字技术对能源消耗的双重效应。而邓荣荣和张翱祥（2022） REF _Ref165315683 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [25]较为系统探讨了数字经济对城市绿色发展影响，通过实证研究发现城市数字经济能够通过构建企业绿色生产模式、优化政府环境监管模式及完善社会环保监督手段三个方面来减少城市环境污染，通过技术创新效应和结构优化效应发挥中介作用，提高城市绿色发展水平，且数字经济对环境污染物排放存在负向空间溢出效应。

本研究遵循数据的可获取性、真实性和系统性原则，建立了衡量数字经济发展水平的指标体系。研究对象为中国2014年至2022年的30个省份（不包括香港、澳门、台湾和西藏）。数据主要来自国家统计局的官方网站、各省的统计年鉴和公报、中国电子信息资料以及《中国经济白皮书》和《中国统计年鉴》。对于部分缺失的数据，本研究采用了线性插值或均值替代的方法进行处理。
（二）绿色发展的指标测度
1.评级体系构建的原则与依据
国内外关于绿色发展的实证研究非常广泛，对绿色发展水平的评估与数字经济的评估一样，需要从多个角度进行考量。当前，研究者们通常采用基于投入产出的数据包络分析法（DEA）及其扩展模型（例如DDF-DEA模型）来评估绿色发展效率。例如，罗宣等（2019）通过超效率SBM模型和Malmquist指数来测算城市的绿色发展效率。在评估方法上，主要结合了指标体系评价和效率测度两种方式。其中，数据包络分析法（DEA）作为一种非参数方法，用于估算生产前沿面上的观测值效率；而随机前沿法（SFA）则是一种参数化方法，具有经济学理论基础，能够提供多阶可导数和参数估计，但依赖于多个假设条件。与此同时，DEA及其衍生模型如DDF-DEA模型，能够处理多产出和多投入的情况。
但当出现投入量过多或者产出量不足的情况时，传统的DEA模型便不再适用。而Tone（2003） REF _Ref165315743 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [26]提出SBM模型中，考虑到了松弛变量，其中超效率SBM 模型则是在普通SBM模型的基础上考虑了非期望产出。因此，文章使用绿色全要素生产率来代替绿色发展水平，选择基于SBM-DEA的GML生产率指数来对各省的绿色全要素生产率进行测算。

2.内生性检验
在本研究中，我们采取了一系列措施来解决内生性问题，以确保研究结果的准确性和可靠性。首先，我们采用了双固定面板模型，并在模型中纳入了可能影响绿色发展的一系列控制变量，以此来减轻内生性问题和由遗漏变量引起的偏差。然而，考虑到可能存在的双向因果关系和遗漏变量问题，我们进一步借鉴了黄小勇（2020）等人的研究方法，选择了固定电话用户数作为数字经济发展指数的工具变量。这一选择基于固定电话用户数与固定电话数量之间的高度正相关性，以及固定电话作为互联网发展基础对数字经济的一定影响，这满足了工具变量与核心解释变量相关性的要求。同时，鉴于互联网信息技术的迅猛发展，人们对于传统通信工具的依赖已大幅降低，固定电话用户数对绿色发展的影响可以忽略不计，这满足了工具变量与随机扰动项不相关的条件。
通过应用两阶段最小二乘法（2SLS）进行实证检验，我们发现固定电话用户数这一工具变量对内生解释变量的回归在1%的水平上显著，p值为0.002，证实了工具变量与数字经济发展水平之间存在显著的相关性。进行工具变量的弱识别检验时，F统计值为15.992，表明固定电话用户数是一个强有力的工具变量。此外，对解释变量内生性的检验显示p值均小于0.05，确认了数字经济发展水平作为一个内生变量，确实需要借助工具变量进行处理。

五、结论与建议
（一）主要结论
在探索数字经济与绿色发展交织的奥秘中，本研究以我国2014至2022年间30个省、直辖市、自治区的丰富面板数据为画布，绘制出一幅经济与生态和谐共生的发展图景。运用基准回归、动态面板模型、空间杜宾模型以及门槛效应等多元分析工具，本文对数字经济如何稳健地、内生地影响区域绿色发展进行了深入的实证剖析，揭示了区域间异质性所带来的独特视角。研究的结论，宛若一幅精妙的画卷，缓缓展开，引领我们洞察数字经济在推动经济社会高质量发展中的新引擎作用，以及它在科技创新、经济增长和供给侧改革中的新动力和新要素角色。得到的结论如下：
第一，中国数字经济对地区绿色发展产生了显著的正面影响，这一点在区域数字经济发展水平与绿色发展之间的统计联系中得到了体现，并在后续的标准回归分析中得到了进一步的确认。通过工具变量法进行的稳定性检验也支持了数字经济推动绿色发展水平提升的结论。
第二，在探讨数字经济对地区绿色发展水平的区域异质性时，我们观察到了一些有趣的现象。尽管数字经济的快速增长在总体上促进了两个主要地区的绿色发展，但东部和中西部地区之间存在明显差异。东部地区的数字经济对绿色发展具有显著的正面影响，而中西部地区则没有表现出这种显著性，这表明了数字经济对各地区绿色发展水平影响的区域性差异。
第三，数字经济对区域绿色发展水平的影响具有显著的空间效应。一个地区的绿色发展水平在很大程度上受到该地区数字经济发展水平的影响。这一点从空间杜宾模型的分析中得到了证实，模型结果表明数字经济的系数显著为正，从而确认了区域数字经济的增长对提升区域绿色发展水平具有重要的正面作用。
第四，通过面板模型检验数字经济对区域绿色发展水平的门槛，我们探讨了科技创新和产业结构升级对其影响的可能性，即数字经济对绿色发展是否可能出现跳跃式的影响。结果显示，当技术创新水平较高时，数字经济对绿色发展具有积极的推动作用。然而，在产业结构水平作为门槛变量的情况下，并未通过门槛检验，因此产业结构水平的门槛效应不成立。
（二）建议
为了能使数字经济对绿色发展有更好的促进作用， 通过本文上述的相关分析结果，从而提出相关建议。
第一，通过异质性分析，我们发现数字经济对东部和中部地区的影响更为深远。然而，在推动绿色经济转型的过程中，这种影响可能会加剧地区之间的不平衡。因此，政府应该增加对西部地区数字化基础设施的资金投入和技术支持，以助其经济发展迈入快车道。这样，各地区之间的发展才能更加平衡。
第二，通过门槛效应检验我们发现，当科技创新水平较高时，数字经济对绿色发展起到了积极的推动作用。因此，我们应当加强对各地区科学技术的培养与发展，注重人才的引进与培养，打造创新团队，并着力加强基础研究的应用，以不断提升自主创新的能力。
第三，数字经济的兴盛对于提升绿色发展具备积极的影响。因此，我们可以借助数字化技术和手段来实现产品的环保标识和监管，以及对系统进行有效的监控和调整。 REF _Ref165316736 \r \h \* MERGEFORMAT [36]与此同时，数字经济的蓬勃发展也会带来环境污染的挑战，但我们可以采取一系列措施，如优化数据中心的能效，从而推动数字经济的可持续发展。

title: 中国区域韧性时空演变及影响因素

sections.text:
中国区域韧性时空演变及影响因素：基于省级面板数据的Spearman-CRITIC与XGBoost-CatBoost-SHAP实证研究
Yile Wang1
摘要
区域韧性与可持续发展密切相关，因为它反映了一个地区在长期转型下维持稳定的经济、社会、生态和基础设施功能的能力。基于2007年至2024年中国省级面板数据，本研究构建了涵盖经济韧性、社会发展韧性、生态环境韧性和基础设施韧性的区域韧性评价体系。采用Spearman-CRITIC模型计算韧性指数，同时应用冷热点分析和核密度估计来考察空间格局和分布动态。进一步使用XGBoost-CatBoost混合模型和SHAP方法来识别潜在影响因素的解释贡献。结果表明，研究期内中国省级韧性总体呈上升趋势，尽管区域差异依然明显。热点主要集中在东部沿海和部分中东部省份，而冷点则间歇性出现在西部和西南部地区。SHAP结果表明，收入水平、民营经济活力和城市化率对模型预测的贡献相对较大，且存在明显的区域异质性。使用替代权重方法进行的稳健性检验支持了主要解释模式的稳定性。这些发现为理解以可持续发展为导向的治理下的区域韧性提升提供了实证证据。
关键词：区域韧性；时空演变；Spearman-CRITIC；可持续发展；XGBoost-CatBoost-SHAP。
引言
可持续发展不仅关乎经济增长。它还关乎一个地区在长期转型期间维持社会稳定、生态安全和公共服务提供的能力 [1]。随着气候变化、资源约束 [2]、产业结构调整和人口流动的不断叠加，区域发展正面临更大的不确定性 [3]。因此，区域韧性成为理解区域可持续发展能力的重要视角 [4]。在中国，各省份在经济基础、公共服务、生态条件和基础设施禀赋方面存在显著差异 [5]。在面临外部冲击和内部转型压力时，其恢复、适应和持续发展的能力也有所不同 [6]。因此，系统测度中国省级韧性，识别其空间格局和相关因素，对于理解区域协调发展和可持续治理具有重要意义 [7]。
现有的区域韧性研究大致可分为三个方向。第一个方向侧重于其概念内涵和测度框架。这些研究通常从经济、社会、生态和基础设施维度评估韧性 [8]。通常构建多维度指标体系，并使用熵权法 [9]、主成分分析 [10] 和因子分析 [11] 等综合评价方法计算韧性水平。由于区域韧性是一个综合概念，单一指标很难捕捉其变化特征。因此，经济、社会、生态和基础设施维度已逐渐成为通用的分析框架 [12]。这些研究为后续的实证分析奠定了基础，并帮助区域韧性研究从概念探讨转向定量评估。
第二个方向更加关注区域韧性的空间格局和动态演变。在构建综合韧性指数后，这些研究通常考察空间集聚、分布演进以及区域差异的来源 [13]。例如，经常使用空间自相关分析来检验高值区或低值区在空间上是否集聚 [14]。冷热点分析可以进一步识别高值或低值集中的局部单元 [15]。核密度估计常用于描述不同年份间韧性水平分布的变化 [16]。一些研究还对区域差异进行分解，以考察区域间和区域内的韧性差距 [17]。该方向的价值在于其从静态测量转向时空分析，使得区域韧性研究能够更好地捕捉韧性水平的空间不平衡和时间变化 [13,17]。
第三个方向侧重于识别与区域韧性相关的影响因素。这些研究通常将区域韧性与城市化、产业结构调整、创新投入等发展条件联系起来，进而考察不同地区韧性水平的差异 [18]。传统研究通常使用计量经济学回归模型来检验变量之间的线性关系，此类模型可以提供有关系数方向和统计显著性的信息 [19]。近年来，机器学习方法越来越多地应用于区域研究中。部分研究开始使用非线性模型来识别变量重要性和复杂关联 [20]。然而，如果没有合适的解释工具，这些方法可能停留在预测阶段，对不同变量如何对模型产生贡献的解释有限 [21]。总体而言，现有研究在测度、时空演变和因素识别方面为区域韧性分析奠定了有益基础。在非正态指标赋权、非线性解释和区域异质性识别等方面仍需进一步深入开展工作 [22]。
[图 1. 研究框架图]
在现有研究的基础上，本文考察了中国省级区域韧性的测度、演变及其解释因素。利用2007至2024年的省级面板数据，本研究构建了区域韧性综合评价体系，并在考虑指标分布特征的情况下测度了韧性水平。随后从空间格局和分布动态两个视角分析了区域韧性的时空演变。在因素分析方面，引入XGBoost-CatBoost混合模型和SHAP方法，以识别不同变量对模型预测的相对贡献。通过这一设计，本文旨在构建一个将综合测度、时空分析和可解释机器学习联系起来的一致性框架。它还为理解中国省级韧性差异及其对可持续发展的启示提供了实证证据。
数据来源与方法
区域韧性测度体系
本研究使用2007至2024年中国省级面板数据构建区域韧性的综合测度体系。由于区域韧性涉及经济表现、社会服务、生态状况和基础设施支撑，因此将其划分为四个子系统：经济韧性、社会发展韧性、生态环境韧性和基础设施韧性 [8,9]。经济韧性主要反映一个地区的经济基础、消费能力、财政能力和产业结构，通过人均GDP、人均社会消费品零售总额、财政自给率和第三产业占GDP比重来衡量。社会发展韧性侧重于就业压力、医疗资源、信息获取和高等教育资源，包括城镇登记失业率、每万人拥有医院床位数、互联网普及率和每十万人高等学校在校生数。生态环境韧性反映了绿化空间、污染排放压力和环境治理投入。基础设施韧性则从供气、供水、道路和公共交通的角度反映公共服务保障能力 [10]。所有指标的缩写、单位和方向如表1所示。

在进行综合赋权和指数测度之前，有必要检查基础指标的分布特征。表2报告了各项指标的描述性统计及KS正态性检验结果。从极值和标准差来看，各省在经济发展、财政能力、污染排放强度和基础设施覆盖方面存在明显的省际差异 [11]。例如，PCGDP和PCRS的最大值与最小值之间存在巨大差距，表明各省经济基础和消费能力差异显著。WEI和SDEI也表现出强烈的离散性，说明各地区面临的生态环境压力存在很大差异。KS检验结果显示，除HBTP和PCURA外，多数指标的p值均低于0.05。这表明样本数据总体上不满足正态性假设 [12]。鉴于此特征，正负指标需要在后续的测度中统一方向。在相关性测度和权重计算中也应使用更适合非正态数据的方法，以减少偏态分布和极端值对综合评价结果的影响。
基于测得的区域韧性指数，本研究进一步构建了一组影响变量，以解释韧性水平差异及其变化的来源。因变量为区域韧性得分，记为RESILIENCE。解释变量包括城市化率（URB）、政府干预强度（GOV）、科技投入强度（INNO）、教育投入强度（EDU）、人均对外开放水平（OPENPC）、金融发展水平（FIN）、数字发展水平（DIG）、民营经济活力（PRI）、居民收入水平（INC）以及社会保障支持力度（SOC）。URB反映了人口集聚与城市化进程。GOV代表地方政府配置公共资源的能力。INNO和EDU分别表示科技投入和教育支持。OPENPC和FIN捕捉外部经济联系和金融服务能力。DIG和PRI描述数字发展和市场活力。INC和SOC对应生活水平和社会保障状况 [18]。这些变量为从经济结构、公共投入、对外开放、市场活力和民生保障等视角解释区域韧性提供了基础，同时也为后续的统计分析和SHAP解释提供了支持 [20]。
